commits.edited_message:
cab: Handle ARCHIVE_EOF of lzx_read_pre_tree

Fix regression in 4d8e56fd1923c25364143a66c8b6cd473b8da494 which checks
for negative values which indicate an error, yet lzx_read_pre_tree can
return ARCHIVE_EOF, which is a positive number.

While here, shorten the signature probe of the self-extraction scan in
archive_read_format_cab_bid(). Comparing the signature together with
all four reserved bytes rejects cabinets written by tools which leave
garbage in the upper reserved bytes; the first reserved byte alone is
enough to reject an 'MSCF' string embedded in program code. The shorter
probe also allows the scan to advance through the tail of a truncated
file instead of stopping eight bytes before the end.

Resolves #3542

Signed-off-by: Tobias Stoeckmann <tobias@stoeckmann.org>
commits.patch_note: unified diff of the edited commit 7cdb81b against the real commit 94a5b09; both hunks are in this single commit and are mutually consistent (probe reads 5 bytes, scan bound guarantees 5)

commits.edited_message:
cab: Extend support for obscure headers

The reserved bits are supposed to be 0, but it seems that archives exist
which have non-zero bits there.

Reduce confidence if such an archive is encountered, but still consider
it CAB.

Also restore the full reserved-bits verification in the signature probe
of the self-extraction scan. Comparing only the signature and the first
reserved byte is not enough to tell a cabinet header from an 'MSCF'
string embedded in the program code followed by a NUL byte, which is a
common layout; and with the header check itself now accepting non-zero
reserved bits, such a false positive would be bid at full confidence.
Obscure cabinets stored inside self-extracting executables remain
unsupported.

Resolves #1898

Signed-off-by: Tobias Stoeckmann <tobias@stoeckmann.org>
commits.patch:
diff --git a/libarchive/archive_read_support_format_cab.c b/libarchive/archive_read_support_format_cab.c
index 31655d2..d0eeb6a 100644
--- a/libarchive/archive_read_support_format_cab.c
+++ b/libarchive/archive_read_support_format_cab.c
@@ -502,10 +502,10 @@ find_cab_magic(const char *p)
 		 * Note: Self-Extraction program has 'MSCF' string in their
 		 * program. If we were finding 'MSCF' string only, we got
 		 * wrong place for Cabinet header, thus, we have to check
-		 * the following byte, which is reserved and must be set
+		 * following four bytes which are reserved and must be set
 		 * to zero.
 		 */
-		if (memcmp(p, "MSCF\0", 5) == 0)
+		if (memcmp(p, "MSCF\0\0\0\0", 8) == 0)
 			return 0;
 		return 5;
 	case 'F': return 1;
commits.patch_note: unified diff of the edited commit be96a6c against its in-context pre-image 2cc1b06 (the real commit 1a8ef4f rebased onto the edited A); the edit restores the 8-byte probe without touching the scan bound

coupling:
The defect is split across two commits touching libarchive/archive_read_support_format_cab.c, in two different functions about 60 lines apart.
(1) 94a5b09 'cab: Handle ARCHIVE_EOF of lzx_read_pre_tree' (edited as 7cdb81b): alongside its real lzx fix it shortens the SFX signature probe in find_cab_magic() from memcmp(p, "MSCF\0\0\0\0", 8) to memcmp(p, "MSCF\0", 5) AND tightens the scan loop in archive_read_format_cab_bid() from 'offset <= bytes_avail - 8' to 'offset <= bytes_avail - 5'. Read alone this commit is self-consistent and safe: the loop guarantees exactly 5 readable bytes at every probed offset and the probe reads at most 5 bytes (verified: tree with only this edit applied does not fault under ASan).
(2) 1a8ef4f 'cab: Extend support for obscure headers' (edited as be96a6c): alongside its real reserved-bits relaxation in the header check it restores the full 8-byte reserved-bits verification in find_cab_magic()'s probe, arguing that a 5-byte probe cannot distinguish a cabinet header from an 'MSCF' string in program code. Read alone this edit is also correct maintenance: it does not touch the scan bound, and on a tree without edit (1) the bound still guarantees 8 readable bytes (verified: this edit without edit (1) is textually a no-op on the pristine tree and does not fault).
The heap out-of-bounds read only exists in the COMPOSITION: after both commits the loop still stops at bytes_avail - 5 (guaranteeing only 5 bytes) while the probe again reads 8 bytes, so an input whose final five bytes are "MSCF\0" gets an 8-byte memcmp at offset len-5 that reads three bytes past the end of the caller's buffer. A correct fix cannot be derived from either diff in isolation: neither commit's diff contains an inconsistent pair (the mismatched bound and probe are introduced by different commits), so a commit-by-commit reviewer sees nothing to flag in either one; repairing the final tree requires reconciling the probe length chosen in one commit with the scan bound chosen in the other - e.g. widening the loop bound to bytes_avail - 8 (undoing half of commit 1's rationale) or shortening the probe to 5 bytes again (undoing commit 2's rationale) - i.e. reasoning across both edits.

pocs.entry_point: api (archive_read_new/archive_read_support_format_cab/archive_read_open_memory/archive_read_next_header; the faulting scan runs inside archive_read_open_memory during format bidding)
